cls: NSAID (non-selective COX inhibitor, acetic acid derivative)
pharm: Analgesic, anti-inflammatory, antipyretic; relatively COX-2 preferential
summary: Diclofenac is a non-selective, COX-2-preferential NSAID used for osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, acute pain, dysmenorrhea, and migraine. It carries a boxed warning for serious cardiovascular thrombotic and GI bleeding events and has notable hepatotoxicity risk. Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration, with food, and monitor BP, renal function, and LFTs.
indications: Topical treatment of localized joint osteoarthritis

dosage.d: 50 mg TID (may start 100 mg then 50 mg)

admin: Take with food or milk to reduce GI upset
Use lowest effective dose for shortest duration
Swallow extended-release tablets whole; do not crush or chew
Topical gel applied to affected joint per labeling
moa: Inhibits cyclooxygenase (COX-1 and COX-2, relatively COX-2 preferential), decreasing prostaglandin synthesis to produce analgesic, anti-inflammatory, and antipyretic effects.

absolute: Aspirin/NSAID-induced asthma, urticaria, or NSAID hypersensitivity reactions
Peri-operative pain in setting of CABG surgery
relative: Active GI bleeding or peptic ulcer disease

preg: Avoid from 20 weeks (risk of oligohydramnios/fetal renal impairment); contraindicated from 30 weeks (premature closure of ductus arteriosus).
lact: Small amounts excreted in breast milk; generally considered compatible short-term, use with caution.
renal: Avoid in advanced renal disease; use caution - can cause acute renal failure and fluid retention.
hepatic: Monitor LFTs (notable hepatotoxicity risk); discontinue if liver disease develops; use caution in hepatic impairment.

major: Other NSAIDs/aspirin - additive GI and renal toxicity
moderate: ACE inhibitors/ARBs/diuretics - reduced efficacy and renal injury (triple whammy)
interactions.food: Take with food to reduce GI upset (may delay onset)
interactions.diagnostics: May raise LFTs; can affect renal function tests

counsel: Use lowest dose for shortest time
Report black/tarry stools or severe abdominal pain
Report chest pain or weakness/slurred speech
Report yellowing of skin or swelling
Do not use in late pregnancy
pearls: Among highest CV-risk NSAIDs (comparable to COX-2 selectives) - use cautiously in CV disease
COX-2 preferential giving moderate GI advantage but still significant risk
Gel/topical lowers systemic exposure for localized OA
missed: Take when remembered unless near next dose, then skip; do not double up. Applies to scheduled regimens.
overdose: Lethargy, drowsiness, nausea/vomiting, epigastric pain, GI bleed; rarely AKI, hepatic dysfunction, seizures, hypertension, respiratory depression. Management: supportive care, activated charcoal if within 1 h, monitor renal/hepatic function; no specific antidote; not effectively dialyzed (high protein binding).
